title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
statement:
Given a sorted array of integers `nums`, remove the duplicates in-place such that each unique element appears only once. The relative order of the elements should be kept the same.

Return the number of unique elements `k` in `nums`.

To get accepted, you must do this by modifying the input array in-place with O(1) extra memory.
constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order.

examples.explanation: Your function should return k = 2, with the first two elements of nums being 1 and 2 respectively.
Your function should return k = 5, with the first five elements of nums being 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4 respectively.

editorial.approach: Use a two-pointer approach. Keep a pointer `i` for the last unique element found. Iterate `j` through the array. When nums[j] !== nums[i], increment `i` and copy nums[j] to nums[i]. Return `i + 1`.

hints: Since the array is sorted, all duplicate elements will be adjacent to each other.
Keep a pointer `i` at index 0. This will track the position of the last unique element.
Iterate another pointer `j` from 1 to `n-1`. Whenever `nums[j] !== nums[i]`, increment `i` and copy `nums[j]` to `nums[i]`.

bruteForceSolution.explanation: Store the unique elements in a temporary Set or array. Copy the unique elements back into the original array and return the count.

optimizedSolution.explanation: Use a two-pointer approach to write unique elements forward in-place, achieving O(1) auxiliary space.

interviewExplanation: A Set approach takes O(n) space. In interviews, O(1) space is required. We maintain a slow pointer `i` for unique values, and a fast pointer `j` to scan. We copy unique elements forward, returning `i + 1` as the count.
